Assessment.content: Asthma exacerbation associated with 2–3 days of wheeze and shortness of breath, cough, afebrile, no sputum, no hemoptysis, no chest pain, exertional limitation, no nocturnal symptoms, history of childhood asthma, inconsistent SABA use, and no spacer or peak flow meter

Plan_of_Care.content: For asthma exacerbation, increase salbutamol to 2–4 puffs every 4 hours initially
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Asthma exacerbation: Increase salbutamol 2–4 puffs q4h initially

Plan_of_Care.content: For asthma exacerbation, prescribe spacer and have pharmacist demonstrate its use
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Asthma exacerbation: Rx spacer; pharmacist to demonstrate use

Plan_of_Care.content: For asthma exacerbation, prescribe peak flow meter and have patient record peak expiratory flow morning and evening for 1 week
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Asthma exacerbation: Rx peak flow meter; record PEF AM and PM x 1 wk

Plan_of_Care.content: For asthma exacerbation, provide safety-net advice to call if high temperature or wheeze worsens
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Asthma exacerbation: Safety-net — call if high temp or wheeze worsens

Plan_of_Care.content: For asthma exacerbation, arrange review in about 1 week, earlier if worse, to discuss peak flow readings and consider additional medication
